title: Systems Manager (SSM) Patch Compliance

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `aws:ssm:compliance` events with `ComplianceType="Patch" status!="Compliant"` into `index=aws`. Confirm UC-4.1.45 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `aws:ssm:compliance` traffic without `ComplianceType="Patch" status!="Compliant"`. Confirm UC-4.1.45 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:ssm:compliance` collected via `Splunk_TA_aws`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=aws sourcetype="aws:ssm:compliance" ComplianceType="Patch" status!="Compliant"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.45_systems_manager_ssm_patc_45"
| sort -_time
description: UC-4.1.45 — Systems Manager (SSM) Patch Compliance: queries AWS `aws:ssm:compliance` for search criteria `ComplianceType="Patch" status!="Compliant"` and returns actor, resource, and region context for compliance review and change validation.
value: On AWS, detecting 'Systems Manager (SSM) Patch Compliance' early shortens cloud incident response and produces defensible audit evidence for identity and change-management controls. UC-4.1.45 drives high-priority compliance alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Use AWS Config rule for patch-compliance or custom automation to export Patch Manager compliance to S3/CloudWatch. Ingest in Splunk. Dashboard compliance % by OU/account. Alert when compliance drops below threshold.
visualization: Table (instance, status), Pie chart (compliant vs non-compliant), Bar chart by patch group.

detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws` with the modular input for `aws:ssm:compliance`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.1.78.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Use AWS Config rule for patch-compliance or custom automation to export Patch Manager compliance to S3/CloudWatch. Ingest in Splunk. Dashboard compliance % by OU/account. Alert when compliance drops below threshold.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:ssm:compliance" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:ssm:compliance" ComplianceType="Patch" status!="Compliant"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.45_systems_manager_ssm_patc_45"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:ssm:compliance` in `index=aws` to detect systems manager (ssm) patch compliance. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_1_45_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Table (instance, status), Pie chart (compliant vs non-compliant), Bar chart by patch group..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of systems manager (ssm) patch compliance so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
